title: When the Prom Burns
premise: Orsen Vane has spent years perfecting invisibility, holding together a household of younger siblings while their mother works nights. When best friend Juniper Sol disappears and leaves only her car keys and a half-burned note in Orsen's locker, the trail leads to the abandoned fairgrounds where their town's annual prom is secretly planned — and to a decades-old cover-up involving the town's founding family. Orsen must choose between protecting Juniper's dangerous secret and telling the truth that could save her, even if exposing it means betraying the friendship and dragging Orsen's fragile family into the light. The story ends with Juniper found alive at the fairgrounds' sealed bomb shelter, the town's buried crime exposed, and Orsen accepting that survival sometimes costs more than silence ever did.
about_author: Ansel Marchetti is the pen name of a former night-shift dispatcher who grew up in a fading mill town and writes about kids who raise themselves. Their short fiction has appeared in several small-press anthologies of contemporary young adult suspense.

chapters.title: Locker Combination
chapters.summary: Orsen Vane's POV. Establish the morning routine: waking siblings, packing lunches, arriving at school invisible. Orsen's careful system of staying under the radar is described with quiet pride. Emotional beat: the comfort of control, and the faint dread that it can't last.

chapters.title: Juniper's Rules
chapters.summary: Orsen and best friend Juniper Sol share a rooftop lunch; her rules for surviving Hollow Creek High are recited like scripture. But Juniper is distracted, asking odd questions about the Vane family's old connection to the Ashford estate. Emotional beat: warmth shadowed by the sense that Juniper is carrying something heavy.

chapters.title: The Empty Desk
chapters.summary: Juniper doesn't show for third period, then not at all. Teachers shrug; her parents assume she's at Orsen's. Orsen covers for her out of habit, then opens their shared locker to find Juniper's car keys and a scorched scrap of paper. Emotional beat: denial curdling into fear.

chapters.title: Keys
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV, night. Unable to sleep, Orsen studies the keys — one is unfamiliar, stamped with a faded fairground logo. The burned note fragment reads only '...prom... they'll know.' Younger sister Wren catches Orsen awake and offers fierce, childish comfort. Emotional beat: the weight of being the one who holds things.

chapters.title: Reported, Dismissed
chapters.summary: Orsen reports Juniper missing; the deputy is polite and useless, hinting Juniper has 'run away before.' Orsen knows that's a lie. The Ashford family name surfaces in the deputy's careful phrasing, and Orsen notices how the room goes quiet. Emotional beat: first taste of a system that protects the wrong people.

chapters.title: Head Down, Grades Up
chapters.summary: Orsen tries to return to routine for the siblings' sake, but school feels like a held breath. Juniper's other friends act strange, rehearsed. One, Theo Marsh, warns Orsen to 'let it go' — then slips a matchbook into Orsen's hand. Emotional beat: isolation deepening, allies uncertain.

chapters.title: What Mom Doesn't Say
chapters.summary: Mother Vane's POV, brief. Home before dawn, she notices Orsen's exhaustion and the missing friend on the news. She almost asks, then works a double instead. A flashback reveals she once worked at the Ashford estate — and was fired the summer of a fire no one discusses. Emotional beat: inherited silence.

chapters.title: The Matchbook
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. The matchbook is from the Cinder Room, a defunct bar beneath the old fairgrounds grandstand. Theo texts coordinates and one sentence: 'She figured out the fire wasn't an accident.' Emotional beat: the case stops being a disappearance and becomes a conspiracy.

chapters.title: Fairgrounds at Dusk
chapters.summary: Orsen and Theo sneak onto the condemned fairgrounds. The grandstand is rotting, but the Cinder Room's cellar door is freshly padlocked — new lock, old door. Someone is keeping people out. Orsen pockets a rusted prom ribbon pinned nearby: Juniper's. Emotional beat: dread sharpening into purpose.

chapters.title: Wren's Question
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV, home. Wren asks why Juniper's mom cried at the laundromat, and Orsen realizes the whole town is watching the Vane kids now. Little brother Denny repeats a playground taunt about 'fire kids.' Orsen snaps, then apologizes. Emotional beat: the family's fragile peace cracking under scrutiny.

chapters.title: The Ashford Archive
chapters.summary: Orsen uses a library volunteer shift to dig: 1987, a prom held at the fairgrounds ended when the grandstand burned, killing one girl — an Ashford cousin. Ruled accidental. Juniper's burned note matches a clipping's headline font. Emotional beat: history repeating, and Juniper knew.

chapters.title: Theo Comes Clean
chapters.summary: Theo confesses: Juniper had been interviewing the dead girl's surviving classmates, including Theo's grandfather, who drove the getaway — no, the get-home — car that night. Grandpa Marsh told Juniper the fire was set, then recanted, terrified. Emotional beat: guilt and loyalty at war.

chapters.title: Someone Was in the House
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV, night. A window is ajar, Denny's drawings disturbed. Nothing stolen. On the doorstep: a photograph of the Vane house, taken that morning. Orsen doesn't tell Mom; instead, Orsen rigs a door alarm from a bike bell and string. Emotional beat: protector mode hardening into something harder.

chapters.title: Deputy Cole's Offer
chapters.summary: Deputy Cole pulls Orsen from class — not to help, but to warn. 'Some doors burn you when you open them.' He mentions Orsen's mother by her maiden name, proving he's been digging too. Emotional beat: the law revealed as a leash, not a shield.

chapters.title: Juniper's Hidden Notebook
chapters.summary: Following Juniper's habit of hiding things in plain sight, Orsen checks the school's trophy case — Juniper's nameplate is loose. Inside: a notebook mapping interviews, names redacted in ash-gray, and a final entry: 'The shelter under the Cinder Room. Friday. If I don't come back, it's Ashford.' Emotional beat: grief and fury fused into resolve.

chapters.title: The Price of Silence
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. A scholarship letter arrives — full ride, contingent on 'community standing.' The same day, an anonymous note warns that troublemakers' families lose things. Orsen understands the machinery: keep quiet, get rewarded. Emotional beat: temptation, and the disgust of recognizing its shape.

chapters.title: Mom's Night Off
chapters.summary: Mother Vane finally sits Orsen down. She tells the truth she buried: in 1987 she saw Lenore Ashford's brother carrying kerosene cans toward the grandstand. She stayed silent to keep her job; the fired girl who spoke up never worked in Hollow Creek again. Emotional beat: generational fear handed down, and Orsen refusing to inherit it.

chapters.title: Allies at the Diner
chapters.summary: Orsen convenes Theo, Wren (insisting), and Juniper's cousin Priya at the all-night diner. They pool what they know: the sealed shelter, the Ashford cover-up, Friday's date circled in Juniper's notebook. Emotional beat: a found-family coalition forming — the first time Orsen stops carrying it alone.

chapters.title: The Grandfather's Tape
chapters.summary: Theo's grandfather, dying and unburdening, plays an old cassette: the night of the fire, voices arguing, a girl's scream cut short. He says the girl didn't die in the fire — she was already dead, and the fire was to hide it. Emotional beat: horror, and the terrible gift of a witness.

chapters.title: Ashford's Smile
chapters.summary: Councilman Elias Ashford corners Orsen publicly, all charm: college recommendations, an internship, 'let the past rest.' Orsen, who has spent years being agreeable to survive, hears the threat beneath the kindness. Emotional beat: the moment invisibility stops being protection and becomes complicity.

chapters.title: Broken Window, Broken Rule
chapters.summary: The Vane house is vandalized — 'STAY DOWN' spray-painted across the door. Mom wants to move; Wren wants to fight; Denny cries. Orsen, who has always absorbed blows quietly, feels something break open instead. Emotional beat: fear transmuting into defiance.

chapters.title: What the Keys Open
chapters.summary: Orsen finally tries the unfamiliar key: it fits the Cinder Room's new padlock. Whoever locked it used hardware Juniper stole from her stepfather's shop — meaning Juniper planned to go in, not be kept out. Emotional beat: hope rekindled — Juniper may have gone underground on purpose.

chapters.title: Into the Cinder Room
chapters.summary: Orsen and Priya descend into the cellar at dawn. Dust, old prom decorations, and a campsite: sleeping bag, water bottles, Juniper's jacket. She's been living down here — or hiding. Scratched into the wall: 'HE'S WATCHING THE HOUSE. DON'T LEAD HIM TO ME.' Emotional beat: relief and guilt colliding.

chapters.title: The Trap of Good Intentions
chapters.summary: Orsen realizes the vandals, the photo, the pressure — all of it was meant to flush Juniper out, and Orsen's investigation may be doing exactly that. Deputy Cole's cruiser passes the fairgrounds twice. Emotional beat: the sickening turn — helping might be hunting.

chapters.title: Radio Silence
chapters.summary: Orsen goes dark: no school, no phone, moving Juniper's campsite supplies and leaving coded chalk marks only Juniper would recognize. The siblings cover with a flu story. Emotional beat: Orsen finally breaking their own rules to protect someone else.

chapters.title: Priya's Discovery
chapters.summary: Priya finds Juniper's real evidence cached in the fairgrounds ticket booth: photos of a sealed ledger from 1987 showing Ashford payouts to witnesses — including Orsen's mother. Emotional beat: betrayal and understanding at once — Mom's silence was bought, not chosen.

chapters.title: Confrontation at the Kitchen Table
chapters.summary: Orsen shows Mom the ledger photo. She weeps, then stands straighter than Orsen has ever seen: 'I was nineteen and scared. You don't get to be scared for me anymore.' She agrees to testify. Emotional beat: the inheritance reversed — the child freeing the parent.

chapters.title: The Deputy's Choice
chapters.summary: Deputy Cole, confronted with the ledger, admits he's Ashford's man — but Juniper once covered for his son, and his conscience has been rotting. He gives Orsen forty-eight hours before Ashford moves on the shelter. Emotional beat: a compromised man's redemption, bought late.

chapters.title: Friday
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. The town prepares its annual prom, oblivious, while Orsen plans the extraction: Priya and Theo as decoys at the dance, Wren and Denny with a neighbor, Mom with a lawyer and the ledger. Emotional beat: calm before the storm, love expressed as logistics.

chapters.title: Ashford at the Door
chapters.summary: Elias Ashford visits the Vane house, flanked by 'contractors.' He offers everything — money, the scholarship, a fresh start — if Orsen hands over Juniper and the evidence. Orsen, the boy who never made waves, looks him in the eye and says no. Emotional beat: the quiet kid's loudest moment.

chapters.title: Decoys
chapters.summary: At the prom, Theo and Priya let themselves be seen asking questions, drawing Ashford's watchers while Orsen slips away in a borrowed janitor's uniform. The gym glitters; the fairgrounds rot in the dark. Emotional beat: courage disguised as ordinary teenagers dancing.

chapters.title: Down
chapters.summary: Orsen descends into the Cinder Room as Ashford's men arrive above. A chase through collapsing cellars; Orsen uses the fairground's old maintenance tunnels — knowledge from Juniper's notebook maps. Emotional beat: terror, and the strange clarity of finally acting instead of enduring.

chapters.title: Juniper
chapters.summary: Orsen finds Juniper barricaded in the old bomb shelter, half-starved, furious and relieved. She reveals the last piece: the 1987 girl was killed by Ashford's father, and Elias has spent his career burying it — including the recent 'accident' that nearly caught Juniper. Emotional beat: reunion as reckoning.

chapters.title: The Fire This Time
chapters.summary: Ashford's men set the grandstand alight to destroy the evidence below — history literally repeating. Orsen and Juniper flee through smoke with the ledger, the tape, and each other, as the fairgrounds that started everything burns again. Emotional beat: survival at its steepest price.

chapters.title: Witnesses
chapters.summary: They emerge into the parking lot where Mom, Deputy Cole, and a state investigator — tipped by Cole — are waiting. Ashford is arrested as the grandstand collapses behind him, his family's myth burning with it. Emotional beat: justice arriving not through one hero, but through everyone who finally spoke.

chapters.title: After the Smoke
chapters.summary: The town reckons: news vans, a reopened 1987 case, classmates who once whispered now asking to help. Juniper recovers in the hospital; Orsen visits daily, their friendship scarred but honest. Emotional beat: the awkward, necessary work of repair.

chapters.title: What Orsen Learned
chapters.summary: Orsen's reflective POV. Invisibility kept the family alive, but silence kept the town sick. Orsen writes a college essay about keys, fires, and the cost of staying down — and reads it aloud to Wren and Denny. Emotional beat: identity rebuilt around truth-telling.

chapters.title: The Prom That Happens
chapters.summary: The town holds a make-up prom at the community center. Orsen goes — not invisible, but visible by choice. Juniper saves them a dance; Theo and Priya hold court; Mom chaperones, laughing. Emotional beat: joy reclaimed, ordinary and hard-won.

chapters.title: Sentencing
chapters.summary: Elias Ashford pleads out; the 1987 case is formally reopened, and the dead girl's name — Marisol Ashford — is spoken publicly for the first time in decades. Orsen places Juniper's rusted prom ribbon on the new memorial. Emotional beat: grief given a name, and a grave.

chapters.title: When the Prom Burns
chapters.summary: Final chapter, Orsen's POV. Summer begins: siblings, a repaired window, Juniper's car running again. Orsen keeps the unfamiliar key on a cord — a reminder that some doors must be opened no matter the cost. Last line: the truth didn't burn them; it set them free. Emotional beat: hard-won peace, forward-looking.
